title: CZECHOSLOVAKIAN PHOTOGRAPHIC E...
reason: Meopta Opemus III enlarger in its original box with manual, Kodak guide and paper; a complete boxed vintage enlarger should appeal to film darkroom users; the title's 'circa 1965' may be early.
findings: Five photos. 1: tall cardboard box printed with the meopta logo and a drawing of an enlarger, 'OPEMUS III' down the side, a flat baseboard panel standing beside it, lot tag 552. 2: box art close-up showing the enlarger with an 'OPEMUS III meopta' plate. 3: 'MADE IN CZECHOSLOVAKIA' and the meopta logo. 4: inside the polystyrene packing: chrome column, grey ribbed lamp house, head with black bellows, carrier arm with black knobs, other black parts (negative carrier or lens panel), a red-brown part (possibly a red filter or safelight), a sealed Dove photo paper pack (reads 'Dove', '240', 'Value Pack'), grey mains cable and plug, and the corner of the Kodak booklet's yellow logo at the bottom edge. 5: Kodak booklet 'Developing Printing Enlarging' (title partly cut off) and the Opemus III instruction booklet. The title is supported: this is a Meopta Opemus III in its original box with manual and extras. The date 'circa 1965' is not supported by any marking in the photos; a web search snippet (photrio.com Opemus III thread, seen 19/10/2026, page itself returned 403 when opened) gave Opemus III production as 1969-75 and 6x6 cm capability, so 'circa 1965' may be early. The enlarging lens is not clearly visible and the number of negative carriers cannot be told. No verified sold price found; one search snippet showed a Melbourne seller asking AU$325 for a used Meopta enlarger listed as 'OPEMUS 11' (probably Opemus II) with two lenses and a filter drawer (https://www.ebay.de/itm/205771383494, seen 19/10/2026, asking price only, page not opened).
condition: Box worn, torn at the top edge and scuffed; polystyrene packing yellowed and chipped; metalwork looks clean; instruction booklets creased. Appears complete but untested; lens, condenser and carriers not confirmed; lamp not shown.
rescore_note: Genuine Meopta Opemus III in its original box with both booklets and photo paper, apparently complete, but these 6x6 enlargers are common, bulky and cheap on the used market; lens and carriers unconfirmed, untested, and 'circa 1965' looks early (forum snippet said 1969 to 75), so modest value.
